newsitem.title: UK: Credit Suisse cuts jobs in London.
newsitem.headline: Credit Suisse cuts jobs in London.

text.p: Swiss banking giant Credit Suisse said on Tuesday it has cut around 30 jobs from its foreign exchange and treasury operations in London.
It said the cuts stemmed from the reorganisation of the bank announced in July, when the bank said it expected to reduce staff by 5,000 worldwide, including 3,500 in its domestic banking operation.
A spokeswoman for Credit Suisse said it could not be more precise about the number of jobs to be lost because it hoped to redeploy a few of the people involved.

She said the loss of jobs in the bank's foreign exchange trading, which market sources put at around half a dozen, came as many players in the market reviewed their operations in the light of the changing market and the looming single European currency.
The spokeswoman said it was likely that further jobs will be lost in the bank's London operations in due course.
Banking sources said the job cuts also involved sales and marketing staff and the bank's Treasury department and meant the forex and treasury areas had been cut by about a quarter.
In a related development, Credit Suisse said it was also reducing staff in its New York operations in foreign exchange trading, sales and operations.
In its July restructuring, Credit Suisse said it would concentrate its corporate and investment banking activities in a reformed Credit Suisse First Boston, under chief operating officer Allen Wheat.

CSFB is not expected to face large job losses as there is little overlap between it and other parts of the bank and given the fact that it underwent a major restructuring, with the loss of around 1,000 jobs worldwide, last year.
Relatively low volatility, tightening spreads, the growth of electronic trading and drives to greater efficiency have forced foreign exchange market participants to review their involvement.
